newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian castorseed eases, overseas buyers stand off.
newsitem.headline: Indian castorseed eases, overseas buyers stand off.

text.p: Castorseed June delivery dropped to 1,178/1,179 per quintal from 1,186/1,187 rupees on fresh speculative selling, floor sources said.
Overseas buying remained slow while higher arrivals at the producing centres prompted bull liquidation.
"Foreign buyers are demanding Indian castoroil at 700/705 dollars per tonne while Indian offers are at 715/720 dollars," said Dilip Thakkar, a leading operator.

Meanwhile groundnut oil moved up from 354/355 rupees to 357/358 rupees per 10 kg on absence of fresh arrivals and shortage of ready stock. Inflow remained low due to a nationwide strike by the transport operators.

Imported palm oil also moved up from 285/286 rupees to 292/293 rupees per 10 kg as transportation of palm oil from Bombay port to the market halted and traders were complaining shortage of ready stock. In Rajkot spot groundnut oil was steady at 540/545 rupees per 15 kg.
The Bombay Oils and Oilseed (ready and forward) markets will remain closed on Tuesday for Hindu festival. The market will reopen for trading on Wednesday.
